verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The market empties out and the pigeons take the square.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone left a glove on the bench, palm up,
still holding the shape of the hand that isn't there.
motifs: the shape of an absent hand

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The last bus fills its windows with orange light—
faces going home, none of them mine,
each one carrying a small unfinished thing.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A dog barks twice at nothing, then gives up—
the whole street settling into what it knows,
lit windows closing one by one like eyes.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Somewhere a kettle starts its low complaint—
steam finding the crack in the window
where morning will come looking for a way back in.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I fold yesterday's paper into a boat,
set it on the sill to wait for rain—
some things want to travel without going anywhere.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light hums to itself, half-forgotten—
a moth keeps testing the same locked door,
patient as anything that mistakes glass for open.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The clock on the stove blinks its false midnight—
nobody left to fix the hour it lost
in some storm years back, still counting wrong.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A neighbor's radio drifts through the hedge,
some song from before I was born—
I hum the parts I don't remember learning.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle forgets it's empty, keeps singing—
I let it, just to hear something
insist on its one note long after truth arrives.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Dust settles on the piano's closed lid—
somewhere under there, a chord
waits like a name I used to answer to.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The porch light burns for no one now—
moths still find their way to it,
faithful to a welcome no one meant.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain fills the gutter with its small opinions,
argues all night about direction—
by morning it's forgotten, and the street looks washed of blame.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog circles the same spot three times before lying down—
some old field it still remembers,
grass that hasn't grown here in years.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A kettle forgets it was ever cold—
steam writes its one word on the window
and is already gone before I read it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep a jar of buttons with no coats—
each one a small stopped clock,
still counting the hours it used to close.
